title: Research: liability considerations for publishing open safety designs
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Publishing safety-equipment designs openly raises product-liability questions; counsel review is an open item in PLAN.md.
objective: Summarise public sources on liability for open-hardware and open-standard publishers (disclaimers, warnings, case law commentary, how standards bodies and open-hardware projects handle it) to brief counsel.
acceptanceCriteria: Clear note that this is not legal advice
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
